newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Akzo profits surge to record in second quarter.
newsitem.headline: Akzo profits surge to record in second quarter.

text.p: Chemicals group Akzo Nobel NV said Thursday its second-quarter earnings surged a surprisingly strong 25 percent to a record 459 million guilders ($222.1 million).

The increase from 367 million guilders ($177.3 million) in the year-earlier quarter put the company well on track to meet its forecast that full-year earnings would top last year's record of 1.318 billion guilders ($636.7 million).
"Akzo Nobel stands by its forecast that net income for 1997 will be higher than in the record year 1996," finance director Jean den Hoed told a news conference.

The company, which was formed through the 1994 takeover of Sweden's Nobel Industries, said second-quarter sales rose 10 percent in cash terms to 6.2 billion guilders ($3 billion), mainly due to an 8 percent increase in sales volumes.
Currency translations had a positive effect of 5 percent on sales, while average selling prices dipped 1 percent. The net of divestments and acquisitions cut sales by 2 percent.
Den Hoed said all four divisions had contributed to the profit increase, but the fibers business was still a serious management headache.
"Despite all the measures taken in the past, operating income still totals only a scant 2 percent of sales...not even sufficient to compensate for the financing charges," he said.
"Really we should generate a 10 percent return on invested capital," he said, adding further restructuring at the division was inevitable and job losses could not be ruled out.

Despite higher launch and R&D costs, operating profits at the Pharmaceuticals division were boosted by higher sales volumes for prescription drugs unit Organon, animal health unit Intervet and raw materials unit Diosynth.
The Organon business unit posted volume gains for contraceptive pills, its new antidepressant Remeron and a new fertility drug, Puregon.

Den Hoed said the rise in contraceptive pill sales marked the first increase since the company's best-selling Marvellon was a 1996 scare that so-called third-generation low-dosage pills raised the chances of fatal blood-clotting.
"It's only a 2 percent growth (in sales volume) but it shows the tide has turned," he said.

Remeron sales had taken off in the United States, more than doubling to eight million guilders ($3.9 million) in the six months following the launch and now had a market share of over 1 percent, he said.
Puregon's sales prospects would be equally good once the drug gained U.S. regulatory approval, he said, adding this was expected in the 1997 third quarter.
Akzo Nobel said earnings of all of its Coatings (paint) businesses improved significantly, reflecting higher sales volumes, cost-saving measures and a recovery in margins.

In the Chemicals division, Polymer Chemicals and Surface Chemistry put in an improved performance thanks to higher volumes and cost cutting, while Catalysts began to reap the cost benefits of past investments.
"It's really a very good performance," commented Peter van Schouten, chemicals analyst at MeesPierson, which upgraded Akzo's stock to strong buy from buy.
"It was absolutely needed, given that the first quarter was a disappointment.
